item.title: Surprisingly complex waves reveal the brain's inner workings
For Twelve Years, Mike Tomlin Built a Minecraft Metropolis
item.description: While coaching professional football, Mike Tomlin quietly spent over a decade constructing a massive digital city block by block. The project reflects an uncommon, analog-style patience, though the lack of documentation leaves its architectural merits entirely unverified.

item.title: Show HN: Strata – an expressive semantic layer that can say no to your LLM
Constructing Functional Ultrasound from the Metal Up
item.description: A meticulous breakdown of building functional ultrasound imaging systems from scratch, exposing the raw engineering beneath layers of modern abstraction. The catch is that calibration overhead can easily swallow your margins before the first clean neural signal appears.

item.title: Revisiting the Geometry of Type: SDF, MSDF, and Slug on Modern GPUs
item.description: As rasterization yields ground to vector approximations on hardware, we weigh the rendering precision of Multi-Channel Signed Distance Fields against the raw compile-time overhead of Slug. The tradeoff remains familiar: subpixel sharpness bought at the cost of shader complexity.

item.title: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS Arrives to Anchor Another Five-Year Cycle
item.description: Canonical releases its first point release for the new long-term support cycle, offering stability to desks weary of rapid churn. The underlying risk remains whether upstream maintenance burdens will outpace local engineering capacity.

item.title: Bild AI (YC W25) Is Hiring a Founding Product Engineer
The AI Race Just Got Awkward
Google Unveils Gemini 4 Argon for Deep-Horizon Coding and Defense Work
item.description: Google's Gemini 4 Argon arrives as a frontier model tailored for long-horizon software engineering and vulnerability patching, leveraging expanded output capacity and aggressive context caching. While early benchmarks highlight impressive multi-step reasoning, widespread utility remains constrained by a selective pilot rollout and the persistent friction of validating autonomous code changes.

item.title: GPT-6.1 Sol Deposes Its Predecessor in Seven Days
item.description: Another week, another iteration, as the seven-day reign of GPT-6 Sol yields to a near-Astra successor that shortens the shelf-life of infrastructure investment even further. The tradeoff is relentless capability gain at the cost of architectural stability.
